title: PACE%2BCode%2BA%2B2023.pdf — section 60
text:
23 ‘Offensive weapon’ is defined as “any article made or adapted for use for causing injury to
the person, or intended by the person having it with him for such use by him or by
someone else”. There are three categories of offensive weapons: those made for causing
injury to the person; those adapted for such a purpose; and those not so made or
adapted, but carried with the intention of causing injury to the person. A firearm, as
defined by section 57 of the Firearms Act 1968, would fall within the definition of
offensive weapon if any of the criteria above apply.
